macro.note: SECTOR is the story here: a 2026 AI-driven MEMORY SUPERCYCLE. DRAM revenue guided ~+51% YoY, NAND ~+45%, HBM ~+70%; DRAM contract prices rose ~90-95% QoQ in Q1 with more into Q2; capacity is reallocating to HBM and prices are expected elevated through 2027. The debate is durability vs cyclical peak — MU's ~$100B and SNDK's ~$42B long-term supply agreements are the bulls' evidence of a longer plateau. Rates ~4.5% are a secondary factor.

decisions.rationale_md: Micron is the cleanest way to own the memory supercycle. Fiscal Q3 printed ~$25 EPS at ~85% gross margin with HBM **sold out**, a data-center run-rate over $100B, and — crucially — ~$100B of multi-year Strategic Customer Agreements that give rare visibility for a deep cyclical. At ~$853 it trades at a ~6x forward P/E. The catch is what that low multiple *means*: it's peak-cycle earnings, and the analyst target range ($361 low → $2,200 high, $1,489 mean) literally is the supercycle-vs-peak debate priced out. The contracted revenue tilts me constructive; the cyclicality keeps the downside band wide. Smart money (gekko 2026-05-08): **Tier 1** — Tepper + 8 trailblazer funds + a politician buy.

review.upside_case: HBM4 ramp + contracted revenue sustain the plateau; re-rate toward high-conviction targets → ~$1,280.

decisions.rationale_md: Broadcom is the highest-quality, lowest-cyclicality name in this basket — and the odd one out: it doesn't make memory. Its engine is custom AI accelerators (XPU/ASIC) for hyperscalers plus AI networking and recurring VMware software. Q2 FY26 revenue +48% with AI-semi revenue +143% to $10.8B, guided to +200% in Q3, FY26 AI ~$56B and 2027 AI reiterated above $100B. At ~$374 it's a ~33x forward P/E but PEG ~0.53 on that growth, Strong Buy with a $513 mean (~+37%). It rides the same AI wave as the memory names without their price-cycle whiplash. Smart money: gekko **Tier 3** (Sundheim & Laffont + 5 trailblazers).

decisions.rationale_md: SK Hynix is a great franchise at an awkward entry point. It's the global **HBM leader** (~56% share) and NVIDIA's primary HBM supplier — the single best-positioned company in the AI-memory supercycle. But 'SKHY' is a **brand-new Nasdaq ADR that IPO'd today (Jul 10)** in a record $26.5B listing at $149; it spiked to ~$194 then fell back to ~$164 with violent post-IPO swings. Two things argue for patience, not chasing: the ADR trades at a ~22-38% premium to the Seoul shares that will be tested when two-way conversion opens **Jul 29**, and legacy fixed-price HBM contracts are capping near-term ASP upside (Q2 op-profit reportedly ~8% below consensus). ADR analyst targets look unreliable this early, so I anchor on the setup, not the tape. HOLD — own the franchise after the premium settles. Not in the gekko US snapshot (Korea-listed until today).

decisions.rationale_md: SanDisk is the highest-torque, highest-variance name here. Since spinning out of Western Digital (Feb 2025) it has become a pure NAND/enterprise-SSD play, and the supercycle has been rocket fuel: fiscal Q3 revenue **+251% YoY** to ~$6B, gross margin 78%, ~$23 EPS, $42B of long-term supply agreements, guiding Q4 EPS to $30-33 — and the stock is up roughly **500% in 2026** (52-week range ~$40 → ~$2,354, now ~$1,355, already ~42% off that high). The ~11.7x forward P/E looks cheap, but NAND is the most volatile memory segment and this is one product on peak-cycle earnings. Torque both ways; treat it as a sized, high-risk position, not a core hold → HOLD. Not in the gekko US snapshot.
